description: A cartoon creature from one signed-distance field (sdf_expr): an egg-shaped body, a round head, `legs` stubby legs on flat feet and a tapering tail curling up behind, melted together with a smooth minimum of width blend, and a few seeded soft lumps on the back; the soles are cut flat at the ground with rounded rims. The bounds follow the parts, so the field is only sampled around the creature. sdf_to_mesh meshes it with edges of feature_size (parts are never made thinner than two edges, so the body stays one piece), decimate thins the mesh where the skin is flat, mesh_repair guards the thinnest parts, and uv_unwrap packs the body's charts into the 0..1 tile. Two dark eye spheres sit on the head as separate pieces. Asserts check that the body is one closed, outward-facing piece without self-intersections, and that the creature stands on its feet: its lowest point on the ground and the points near the ground spread over at least 0.3 body_size.

head.desc: size of the head next to the body

legs.desc: number of legs, spread evenly around the belly

tail.desc: length of the tail next to the body; 0 leaves it off

blend.desc: how softly the parts melt into each other (m)

feature_size.desc: size of the smallest feature kept (m), at least body_size / 50: the skin is meshed at this edge length, then thinned where it is flat

seed.desc: random seed of the bumps and the pose of the legs

shape.note: the bounds hold the parts (smooth joins grow them by up to a quarter of their width); sdf_to_mesh adds two edge lengths around them

bounds_max: =max(1.01, 0.86 + 0.5 * head, 0.62 + 0.6 * tail) * body_size + 0.25 * max(blend, 2 * max(feature_size, body_size / 50))

skin_lean.note: thinned where the skin is flat (it moves less than a tenth of the edge length), to no fewer than 3000 triangles. Workaround for speed: uv_unwrap takes about 2 s on the full mesh, under 1 s on this one

skin_repair.note: workaround: where a part is barely two edge lengths thick, sdf_to_mesh can leave zero-area or crossing faces and decimate can then split a seam open; mesh_repair closes and removes them (nothing to do at the defaults)

body_uv.note: chart_smoothing: the thinned mesh is charted on a smoothed copy, so no chart folds

eye_right.note: on the head (radius r = 0.38 body_size head, centre 0.42 body_size + 0.55 r ahead and 0.86 body_size + 0.3 r up), 0.85 r out from its centre towards (0.85, 0.26, 0.45), lowered like the creature (k in shape)

center: =(0.86 + 0.198 * head) * body_size - max(0.02 * body_size, max(feature_size, body_size / 50))

on_ground.note: where a sole is narrower than the mesh's cells, its lowest point can sit a little above the ground: this puts the lowest point exactly on it (no move at the defaults)

contact.note: how far apart the points near the ground lie (within half an edge length of it), for the standing promise

creature.label: Blob creature
creature.description: The creature standing on the origin and facing +X, its soles at y = 0: the body as one closed, outward-facing mesh with uv (its charts packed in the 0..1 tile) in the skin material, and two eye spheres, with the sphere's own uv, in the eye material.
